topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing its focus on the mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition and pattern receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of innate sensing by defining PAMPs and DAMPs and detailing the genetic basis and cellular localization of pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: PRR families, downstream signaling, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific pattern recognition receptor systems, covering Toll-like receptor functions and cascades alongside alternative cytosolic sensors and the inflammasome pathway.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator production, cell trafficking, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate local leukocyte extravasation and lymphatic drainage while also detailing the severe consequences of uncontrolled systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, how tissues repair or scar, and the causes and protective functions of chronic inflammatory states.

topics.label: Conclusion of the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing for the session and previews the subject of the next lecture.
